newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hits session high, jumpstarted by NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hits session high, jumpstarted by NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures jumped to new session peaks on a further technical bounce from its seven-month lows and after NYMEX crude and gasoline opened sharply higher on the back of inventory data, traders said.
"I think it's the APIs and we have the added volatility because of the expiry of the (NYMEX) products on Friday," said Charles Gray, energy analyst at Prudential Bache in London.
"A lot of people were short...and the APIs helped swing a few fence-sitters off the fence," he said, referring to pre-expiry short covering as well as bullish seasonal factors in gasoline.
At 1513 GMT, April Brent was up 31 cents at $19.76 a barrel. Gas oil, with heating oil demand in decline, lagged the complex, and traded only 75 cents higher at $169.50 a tonne.
Today's US Energy Information Administration data showed a greater drawdown in gasoline, of 3.8 million barrels, than last night's American Petroleum Institute decline of 3.2 million.
EIA also said crude stocks fell, by 100,000 barrels, while the API reported an increase of 516,000 barrels.
But Gray warned that unless Brent crude showed further momentum later this afternoon, the rally may prove nothing more than a technical bounce in the larger, two-month downtrend.
